qt: to the Commission Asger Christensen (Renew) Subject:

Danish EU-approved stallion stations face significant differences in fees for the same mandatory certification of breeding material, as well as challenges relating to the transfer of stallions between approved semen collection centres in different Member States. These differing conditions may affect the competitiveness of Danish businesses and their access to the single market. 1.

What is the Commission’s view on the fact that the fee for the same mandatory certificate, issued based on the same digital processing and laboratory results, may vary significantly between Member States, given that Article 82 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 stipulates that the fee must not exceed the costs incurred by the authorities? At the same time, how does the Commission assess the extent to which such differences may affect companies’ ability to apply for EU authorisation and thus participate on an equal footing in the single market?

How does the Commission interpret Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2020/686 in relation to the movement of stallions between authorised semen collection centres in different Member States? Can a stallion be moved directly between such stations without further quarantine or testing, provided it meets relevant health requirements and has undergone the required routine tests with negative results?
